question: Compare memory bandwidth of the Apple M4 Pro and M5 Pro.

message.content: The Apple M5 Pro has a memory bandwidth of 307GB/s, which is an increase from the M4 Pro's 273GB/s [1][5]. This improvement in memory bandwidth allows for faster data transfer between the CPU and GPU, benefiting workloads that rely heavily on both components [1].

sources.title: Apple MacBook Pro Comparison: M4 Pro vs M5 Pro

passages.heading: Memory bandwidth and RAM
passages.text:
### Memory bandwidth and RAM

Apple also increased the memory bandwidth on the M5 Pro, from 273GB/s on the M4 Pro to 307GB/s. That means the unified memory can move data faster between the CPU and GPU, which helps in workloads that rely on both.

Both machines start with 24GB of RAM, but the maximums have changed. The M4 Pro tops out at 48GB, and the M5 Pro goes up to 64GB. If you are buying new and know you need more headroom for larger creative projects or heavier local AI work, that higher memory ceiling does make the M5 Pro more flexible.

passages.heading: Lightroom Classic
passages.text:
## Lightroom Classic

Photo editing was one of the least dramatic parts of the comparison. In Lightroom Classic, both machines felt about the same for normal interaction such as adjusting exposure and moving through the library.

Importing 500 RAW photos and creating initial previews took 18 seconds on both. Exporting 50 photos to JPEG took 9 seconds on the M4 Pro and 7.23 seconds on the M5 Pro. 200 photos took 34 seconds vs 27.96, and all 500 took 1:15 vs 1:07.

So yes, the M5 Pro is faster. But Lightroom is one of those applications where both machines are already so strong that the difference often feels minor.

passages.heading: The best value in the lineup
passages.text:
## The best value in the lineup

Even though it may not be worth upgrading from an M4 Pro, the M5 Pro still comes out looking very strong when compared with the rest of Apple’s Mac lineup. After testing the M5 Pro alongside machines like the M5 Max, M4 Max, and standard M4, the M5 Pro felt like the best balance of performance and price.

The Max chip is definitely more powerful, but it also costs quite a bit more. And in longer tests, throttling still showed up. In a lot of shorter tests, the M5 Pro and M5 Max were actually fairly close. That makes the extra cost of the Max harder to justify unless you truly need that additional headroom. I go deeper on that in my M5 Pro vs M5 Max comparison.

passages.heading: Memory
passages.text:
### Memory

[edit]
The M4 is packaged with LPDDR5X unified memory, supporting 120GB/sec of memory bandwidth. The SoC is offered in 8GB, 12GB, 16GB, 24GB, and 32GB configurations, with the 8GB and 12GB configuration only being available on the iPad. <sup>[3]</sup>

The M4 Pro is available with up to 64GB unified memory (Mac Mini) with a theoretical maximum bandwidth of 273GB/sec.<sup>[12]</sup> The M4 Max is capable of addressing up to 128GB unified memory, with over half a terabyte per second (546GB/sec) of memory bandwidth, with a slightly reduced bandwidth (410GB/sec) for the binned 32-core M4 Max.<sup>[13]</sup>

passages.heading: Memory
passages.text:
### Memory

[edit]
All M5 chips use a unified memory architecture, where CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine share the same single pool of LPDDR5X memory.

The base M5 offers up to 32 GB of unified memory with a theoretical maximum bandwidth of 153.6 GB/s (LPDDR5X at 9600 MT/s), a nearly 30 percent increase over M4.<sup>[2]</sup> The M5 Pro supports up to 64 GB with a theoretical maximum bandwidth of up to 307 GB/s, and the M5 Max supports up to 128 GB, with a theoretical maximum bandwidth of up to 460 GB/s for the 32-core GPU configuration and 614 GB/s for the 40-core GPU configuration.<sup>[3]</sup>

passages.heading: Performance
passages.text:
## Performance

[edit]
Apple's claimed performance improvements, based on internal benchmarks conducted in September 2025 (for M5) and February 2026 (for M5 Pro and M5 Max), are summarized below.<sup>[2]</sup><sup>[3]</sup>

**M5 (vs. M4):**

- CPU multithreaded performance: up to 15% faster
- Overall GPU performance: up to 30% faster
- Ray-tracing GPU performance: up to 45% faster
- Peak GPU AI compute: over 4× faster

**M5 Pro (vs. M4 Pro):**

- CPU multithreaded performance: up to 30% faster
- Overall GPU performance: up to 20% faster
- Ray-tracing GPU performance: up to 35% faster
- Peak GPU AI compute: over 4× faster
- LLM prompt processing: up to 3.9× faster<sup>[18]</sup>

**M5 Max (vs. M4 Max):**
